newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLO CURVE SEEN FLATTENING AGAIN ON DLR STRENGTH.
newsitem.headline: OLO CURVE SEEN FLATTENING AGAIN ON DLR STRENGTH.

text.p: The curve of yields on Belgian linear bonds could continue its recent flattening after the Bundesbank decided on Tuesday to leave its repo rate unchanged at 3.0 percent, dealers said.

The dollar/mark exchange rate DEM= remained the main variable in the movements of the yield curve, which flattened sharply in the past two weeks as the dollar rally led to expectations of an imminent German rate hike DE-INT.
Half of that flattening move has been corrected since, but dealers said the Bundesbank decision to leave the repo rate unchanged could set off a new series of flattening trades.
"The flattening trend is not over yet," said Indosuez Belgium dealer Dimitri Belpaire.
The two year-10 year OLO yield spread BEVIEW, at 212 bp at the start of July, narrowed to 177 bp on August 5, then widened back to 192 bp on Monday.
In late morning trade on Tuesday the two-10 year differential had narrowed to 188 bp again.

The movements in the three month-10 year spread have been more pronounced, but that was due largely to a short spike in Belgian money market yields TTFBXL, itself the consequence of a weakening of the Belgian franc.
Dealers said that if the dollar made a new attempt at breaking above 1.90 to the mark, the flattening trend would regain full force.

Fuel for such a move could come from U.S. economic indicators this week. U.S. unit labour costs and productivity data are due at 1400 GMT today, on Wednesday the market awaits retail sales and producer price data.

Meanwhile, money market yields were bid slightly higher ahead of the weekly T-bill auction, where 126.580 billion francs is at maturity amid talk that the Treasury will be seeking more funding than usual.
The franc hovered just below 20.65 to the mark.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
